last_completed_unit.target: Cargo vendored dependency integrity metadata suitable for ordinary repository-file transport
last_completed_unit.finding: Official Cargo documentation states that directory sources are suitable for checking vendored dependency source into source control and that each crate has an associated .cargo-checksum.json metadata file protecting against accidental modifications. Official Cargo API documentation identifies SHA-256 file checksums in that metadata and requires it for directory-source package loading.
last_completed_unit.verified_scope: Vendored Cargo directory-source artifacts have documented per-crate integrity metadata in ordinary files and are designed for source-control transport.
last_completed_unit.not_verified_scope: Malicious-tamper security, Chat-native execution of cargo vendor/Cargo, or end-to-end richer-mode parity.

source_scope: Current required repository controls for open_source, current own LATEST, SHA-only note-main identity, and exactly one official Cargo documentation search/lookup set limited to doc.rust-lang.org Cargo source-replacement/directory-source/checksum documentation.
scope_guard: This source-qualified finding supports only ordinary repository-file transport plus accidental-modification integrity metadata. It does not satisfy the Phase-1 no-residual-execution gate.

frontier.current_target: Determine whether a pre-existing Cargo vendored directory source can be consumed fully offline after repository checkout, without registry/network access, while preserving the distinction between artifact transport and Cargo process execution.
frontier.next_unit: After fresh required-control bootstrap and successful SHA-only freshness sequence, perform exactly one official Cargo documentation lookup for offline consumption of an already-vendored directory source. Verify only the network/registry dependency of consuming prebuilt vendored files; do not claim scheduled Chat can execute Cargo.
